chapterTitle: Tangents and Angles of a Circle
modelAnswer: (i) angle OBA = 90 degrees, because AB is a tangent at B and OB is the radial segment to the point of contact, and the tangent and radial segment are perpendicular to each other. (ii) angle OCB = 90 degrees, for the same reason at C. (iii) In quadrilateral OBAC the interior angles sum to 360 degrees, so angle BAC = 360 - 90 - 90 - 120 = 60 degrees. (iv) AB = AC since the two tangents drawn to a circle from the outside point A are equal in length, so triangle ABC is isosceles with vertex angle 60 degrees; the base angles are (180 - 60)/2 = 60 degrees, so angle ABC = 60 degrees.

chapterTitle: Tangents and Angles of a Circle
modelAnswer: Let chord AB touch the inner circle at M and chord CD touch the inner circle at N. Join OM and ON. Since a tangent and the radial segment to the point of contact are perpendicular, OM is perpendicular to AB and ON is perpendicular to CD, and OM = ON because both are radii of the inner circle. The perpendicular from the common centre to a chord of the outer circle bisects that chord, so AM = AB/2 and CN = CD/2. In right triangles OMA and ONC, hypotenuse OA = OC (radii of the outer circle) and OM = ON, so the triangles are congruent and AM = CN. Hence AB = CD.

chapterTitle: Tangents and Angles of a Circle
modelAnswer: Let the radii be r1, r2 and r3. Since each pair of circles touches externally, each distance between centres equals the sum of the two radii. The three centre distances are in the ratio 2:3:4 with perimeter 36 cm, so they are 8 cm, 12 cm and 16 cm. Then r1 + r2 = 8, r2 + r3 = 12 and r1 + r3 = 16. Adding gives 2(r1 + r2 + r3) = 36, so r1 + r2 + r3 = 18. Hence r1 = 18 - 12 = 6 cm, r2 = 18 - 16 = 2 cm and r3 = 18 - 8 = 10 cm.

chapterTitle: Tangents and Angles of a Circle
keyPoints: A tangent line is perpendicular to the radial segment at the point of contact -- the stone's flight path (tangent) meets the radius (string) at a right angle.

The radius, the tangent segment travelled, and the line from the centre to the landing point form a right triangle, solved with the Pythagorean theorem: (tangent)^2 = (distance from centre)^2 - (radius)^2.
modelAnswer: The string of length 3 feet is the radius of the circular path, with Ali at the centre O. When the string breaks, the stone flies off along the tangent to the circle at the point where the string broke (a tangent line is perpendicular to the radial segment at the point of contact, so the stone's straight-line path is at right angles to the radius). Let $T$ be the point where the string broke and $H$ the point where the stone hits, 5 feet from Ali. Triangle $OTH$ is right-angled at $T$ (radius $\perp$ tangent), with $OT=3$ ft (radius) and $OH=5$ ft (given). By Pythagoras' theorem, $TH^{2}=OH^{2}-OT^{2}=5^{2}-3^{2}=25-9=16$, so $TH=4$ ft. The stone covered a distance of 4 feet along the tangent.
stem: Ali is whirling a stone tied with a string of length 3 feet. All of a sudden string is broken and the stone moves along tangent direction of circular path and hits a point 5 feet away from Ali. Find the distance covered by the stone.
